name: Château Fontebride 2014
text:
## Château Fontebride 2014 (375 ml)

**The story.** Fontebride is the second wine of Château Haut-Bergeron in [Sauternes](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Ch%C3%A2teau+Haut-Bergeron,+Sauternes,+France&t=k). It carries the name of an old Sauternais family who sold their vineyard to the Lamothes, Haut-Bergeron's owners ([Guide Hachette des Vins](https://www.hachette-vins.com/guide-vins/les-vins/ch-fontebride-2014-2017/201715804), in French). The Lamothe family has been in Sauternes since 1820 ([Guide Hachette des Vins](https://www.hachette-vins.com/guide-vins/les-vins/ch-fontebride-2014-2017/201715804)).

**The house: Haut-Bergeron.** The estate says it has won 118 medals since 1964, 68 of them gold, which makes it the most decorated property in Sauternes. Some of its vines survived [phylloxera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylloxera) and are now over 100 years old; since 1996 these "vieilles dames" have made a special 100% [Sémillon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A9millon) cuvée. In 1990 the family bought a parcel lying between the two branches of the Ciron river, "a little island", where noble rot develops prodigiously ([Château Haut-Bergeron](https://www.chateauhautbergeron.com/), in French).

**Sauternes.** [Sauternes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauternes_%28wine%29) is made from Sémillon, Sauvignon Blanc and Muscadelle grapes shrivelled by [noble rot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noble_rot), the fungus *Botrytis cinerea*, which concentrates their sugar and flavour. It was Dutch traders in the 17th century who first pushed the region towards sweet white wine. By the late 18th century its fame was international: [Thomas Jefferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson) was an avid fan, and he recorded that [George Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington), after tasting [Château d'Yquem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_d'Yquem), ordered 30 dozen bottles ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauternes_%28wine%29)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [Bordeaux sweet wine vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/bordeaux-sweet) calls 2014 "a triumph for Sauternes": some botrytis in September and plenty in late October, with some observers calling it the best vintage since the turn of the century.

**What the critics say for 2014.**
- **[Guide Hachette des Vins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guide_Hachette_des_Vins), 2017 edition: listed** ("vin cité"). Different from the grand vin: crystalline gold, a fine, elegant nose between white flowers and gingerbread; soft and suave on the attack, fresh and spicy on the finish with a touch of curry. "A harmonious Sauternes to keep for the aperitif." (My translation.)
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 92.0** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is twelve years old, and your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2018 to 2027. Half bottles age faster than full ones, so drink this in the next year or so. Serve it well chilled, at 8 to 10°C; no need to decant.

**Food.** Hachette suggests it as an aperitif. It is also classic with foie gras, with blue cheese such as [Roquefort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roquefort), or with a peach or apricot tart.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Fontebride or Haut-Bergeron at the moment.

**Curious details**
- **Dreaming of it in captivity.** The journalist [Jean-Paul Kauffmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jean-Paul_Kauffmann), held hostage in Lebanon for three years, said he often caught himself dreaming of good wines, among them Haut-Bergeron. He wrote about the estate and "the excellent Robert Lamothe" in his book *Voyage à Bordeaux* ([Château Haut-Bergeron](https://www.chateauhautbergeron.com/)).
- **A swap with Yquem.** To consolidate their vineyards, the Lamothes swapped parcels of equal quality with their illustrious neighbour, Château d'Yquem, gaining a 60-are "nugget" ([Château Haut-Bergeron](https://www.chateauhautbergeron.com/)).
- **Counterfeit in reverse.** For some years an unscrupulous merchant bought Haut-Bergeron and sold it dressed in the labels, capsules and corks of one of the appellation's most famous châteaux, until the courts stopped him ([Château Haut-Bergeron](https://www.chateauhautbergeron.com/)).
- **Lucky nines.** Almost every vintage ending in 9 has been exceptional for the estate: 1929, 1949, 1959, 1969, 1979, 1989, 1999 and 2009 ([Château Haut-Bergeron](https://www.chateauhautbergeron.com/)).
